checks.analysis: The coordinate box is the actual four-dimensional real box |y_i|<r/4. The proof uses the Euclidean identity norm(y)^2=sum_{i=0}^3 y_i^2, not the product/sup norm. Each square is less than (r/4)^2, hence the sum is less than r^2/4 and therefore r^2 for r>0. Nonnegativity of norm(y) and positivity of r justify recovering norm(y)<r from the square inequality. The radius r/4 is conservative and uniform.

For every real coordinate tuple x in that box, WithLp.toLp 2 x produces an element of the actual KSSpace with exactly those coordinates. The proof feeds the unchanged coordinate inequalities into the Euclidean bound. It does not need an assumed coverage map or identify different norm instances.

Equality on the positive-radius physical spinor ball becomes equality of the two literal forward-substituted polynomials on the contained real coordinate box. The imported positive-radius real-open-box theorem applies with r/4>0, and proved injectivity of the forward polynomial map yields equality of the original independent-spinor-variable polynomials. No global real evaluation equality is supplied as a hidden input.

The real-invariance premise quantifies over a,b with a^2+b^2=1 and only those y with norm(y)<r, for a fixed positive r. For each unit complex u, the proof uses a=u.re and b=u.im; the norm-squared identity gives the unit real-pair constraint. At each y in the same ball, physical covariance and inverse-substitution evaluation rewrite precisely the two evaluations in hreal.

The local polynomial statement evaluates P at the transformed point as part of its explicit equality hypothesis. P is a globally defined polynomial, so no additional transformed-point domain condition is needed by this statement. The proof does not assume global invariance or extend an arbitrary local function. Applications to local analytic functions must separately provide the displayed polynomial-invariance hypothesis.

For each unit u, local spinor-ball extensionality gives literal equality of ksPolynomialCircleAction u (ksRealPolynomialToSpinor P) and that same transformed polynomial. The final theorem passes exactly this equality to the reviewed all-unit-phase support lemma and concludes d0+d1=d2+d3 for every d in the support of ksRealPolynomialToSpinor P. Neither a replacement polynomial nor assumed support balance appears.
